"Create the first playable prototype of LEGACY OF ETERNIA.

Genre: Isometric 2D fantasy MMORPG.
Visual style: Detailed 16-bit pixel art inspired by classic Lineage II Interlude.

WORLD:

- A medieval fantasy starting village.
- Surrounding green forest.
- Stone roads, houses, NPCs and decorative objects.
- Isometric camera with a fixed 3/4 perspective.

PLAYER:

- Human warrior with sword and armor.
- Character movement using a virtual joystick.
- Smooth 8-direction movement.
- Idle, walking, attacking and death animations.

GAMEPLAY:

- Real-time combat.
- Target selection.
- Health and mana bars.
- Experience and leveling.
- Three monster types: Wolf, Skeleton and Orc.
- Monsters respawn after being defeated.
- Monsters drop gold and equipment.

INTERFACE:

- Mobile landscape orientation.
- Virtual joystick on the left.
- Attack and skill buttons on the right.
- Character status, inventory and minimap.
- MMORPG-style interface.

MULTIPLAYER ARCHITECTURE:
Design the project for future online multiplayer.
Use a server-authoritative architecture where possible.
Prepare player identity, synchronized positions, health, combat and shared world state.
Do not simulate other human players with bots or pretend offline gameplay is multiplayer.

First priority: Generate a stable, playable prototype. Do not add unnecessary features until the core gameplay works.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a stable, playable first prototype of LEGACY OF ETERNIA, an isometric fantasy MMORPG-style game, with core movement, combat, progression, loot, and UI.
- Prepare an honest server-authoritative multiplayer foundation without simulating human players or claiming multiplayer is implemented.

## Requirements
- Medieval starting village, surrounding forest, roads, houses, NPCs, decorations, and fixed 3/4 isometric view with detailed pixel-art-inspired visuals.
- Human warrior with 8-direction movement, joystick and keyboard controls, and idle/walking/attacking/death states.
- Real-time combat, target selection, HP/MP, XP/leveling, Wolf/Skeleton/Orc enemies, respawns, gold and equipment drops.
- Mobile landscape-oriented MMORPG-style UI with joystick, attack/skill buttons, status, inventory, and minimap.
- First priority is core playable stability; avoid unnecessary features.
- Do not fake multiplayer or other human players.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game as a standalone HTML5 Canvas prototype in `index.html`, with no framework or external game dependencies.
- Keep gameplay explicitly single-player until a server transport exists; include player identity, command-send seam, and versioned authoritative snapshot handling.
- Use WASD/arrows and touch joystick for movement; attacks require enemies to be within range.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added playable village/forest canvas world with isometric camera, pixel-style player, NPCs, houses, roads, trees, rocks, and decorations.
- Added movement, targeting, melee and Cleave combat, enemy aggro/attacks, death/return, XP and levels, drops/collection, respawns, potions, inventory, quest counter, status UI, and minimap.
- Added stable session player ID and disconnected multiplayer command/snapshot interface; no fake players.
- Documented controls and multiplayer status in `README.md`.
- Verified JavaScript syntax with `node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js`; browser loaded without console errors after fixing favicon 404.

### Blocked
- Browser automation attempt did not confirm a successful kill/combat loop; the movement direction/duration likely failed to approach the nearest wolf. No other blocker.

## Next Move
1. Inspect latest `screenshots/legacy.jpg` and use browser automation to verify movement, target selection, attack, monster defeat/drop pickup, and inventory.
2. Fix any issues discovered, then run `node --check` and browser console checks again.
3. Keep multiplayer clearly identified as a disconnected foundation, not implemented online play.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation and interface.
- `README.md`: How to run/play and multiplayer architecture notes.
- `screenshots/legacy.jpg`: Latest browser capture for visual inspection.

- Local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; browser URL is `http://localhost:3002`.

## Objective
- Continue developing LEGACY OF ETERNIA as a playable game, preserving its existing world, characters, graphics, and controls.
- Complete and validate Stage 2 combat, monster AI, progression, loot, inventory, and interface.

## Requirements
- Preserve existing locations, characters, graphics, and controls; do not recreate the game.
- Implement real-time melee combat, tap-to-target, sword animation, damage calculation, critical hits, monster health bars, and cooldowns.
- Monsters patrol, detect and attack nearby players, return to spawn when players leave, and respawn after death.
- Award XP on kills; support levels 1–20 with increasing health and attack power, level-up notification, and visual effect.
- Monsters drop gold and have a chance to drop weapons, armor, or accessories; drops can be collected by tapping; provide inventory.
- Show target details, enemy HP, player HP/MP, XP progress, and damage numbers.
- Keep mechanics functional, mobile performance reasonable, and style consistent with existing isometric pixel art.

## Decisions
- Retain the standalone Canvas implementation in `index.html` and build on existing gameplay rather than replacing it.
- Keep multiplayer transport disconnected and do not simulate other human players.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing prototype has movement, targeting, melee and Cleave combat, enemy aggro/attacks, HP/MP/XP, leveling, loot, inventory, respawns, minimap, and HUD.
- Added monster patrol movement, return-to-home behavior, armor mitigation, tap-range prompt for drops, a level-up glow effect, equipment state, and a `collectDrop` helper.
- Updated basic attacks to include level and equipped weapon/accessory attack bonuses.

### Active
- Finish the `hitMob` loot/progression changes: the attempted replacement did not apply, so existing loot still uses the old `name` format and old drop logic.
- Resolve consistency between existing loot drops and the updated `drawDrop`/`collectDrop`, which now expect `d.item`.
- Complete the level cap at 20, leveling stat/attack scaling, critical-hit handling, equipment drops and equipping, and actual tap-to-collect input.
- Update inventory rendering for structured equipment data; add critical-hit styling as desired.
- Validate syntax and browser gameplay, including mobile interaction.

### Blocked
- Current partial edits have a data-shape mismatch: existing `hitMob` generates item drops with `name`/`icon`, while updated `drawDrop` reads `d.item.slot`; rendering an item drop may throw an error.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current `index.html` and fix item-drop data consistency before testing.
2. Complete kill rewards, randomized gold and weapon/armor/accessory drops, tap pickup, inventory/equipment effects, critical hits, and the level-20 cap.
3. Run JavaScript syntax checks and browser tests covering combat, patrol/aggro/return/respawn, leveling, loot, inventory, and mobile controls.
4. Update `README.md` if controls or gameplay behavior change.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Full game implementation, UI, and current Stage 2 changes.
- `README.md`: Controls and single-player/multiplayer-foundation notes.
- `screenshots/verified-combat.png`: Earlier browser screenshot of a verified combat and loot pickup loop.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. Previously noted status: modified `README.md`; untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`.

## Objective
- Continue developing LEGACY OF ETERNIA as a playable game, preserving its existing world, characters, graphics, and controls.
- Finish and validate Stage 2 combat, monster AI, progression, loot, inventory, and interface.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing single-player Canvas implementation in `index.html`; do not recreate the game.
- Support melee and Cleave combat, targeting, sword animation, damage and critical hits, enemy health bars, cooldowns, and player HP/MP/XP.
- Monsters patrol, aggro nearby players, return home when players leave, and respawn after death.
- Award XP and scale health and attack through level 20, with level-up notification and visual effect.
- Monsters drop gold and may drop equippable weapons, armor, or accessories; support nearby tap pickup and inventory.
- Keep gameplay functional, mobile performance reasonable, and visuals consistent with the existing isometric pixel art.
- Keep multiplayer transport disconnected and do not simulate other human players.

## Decisions
- Build on the existing single-player prototype and retain its standalone Canvas implementation.
- Keep a transport seam, but do not connect multiplayer or invent remote players.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented movement, targeting, melee and Cleave combat, enemy aggro and attacks, HP/MP/XP, leveling, loot, inventory, respawns, minimap, and HUD.
- Added monster patrol and return-home behavior, armor mitigation, level-up visual effects, and equipment attack/defense bonuses.
- Added critical hits and styling, structured equipment drops, randomized gold, nearby tap-to-pickup, and pack-capacity handling.
- Added equipment slots and equip-from-inventory interaction; capped progression at level 20.
- `node --check /tmp/opencode/game.js` passed after extracting the inline script from `index.html`.

### Active
- Validate current gameplay and edge cases in a browser, including equipment, combat, AI, progression, drops, and mobile input.
- Update `README.md` controls: it still says to walk over equipment drops, but nearby drops can also be tapped and packed items can be tapped to equip.

### Blocked
- Browser smoke test did not complete: headless Chromium produced DBus/zygote errors and no test-results output.

## Next Move
1. Retry browser validation with a functioning browser automation setup or a simpler Chromium invocation.
2. Check combat, critical hits, patrol/aggro/return/respawn, level-20 cap, loot pickup/equipping, and touch controls.
3. Update `README.md` controls to describe tap pickup and equipping packed items; fix any issues validation reveals.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Full game implementation and current Stage 2 changes.
- `README.md`: Controls and multiplayer-foundation notes.
- `screenshots/verified-combat.png`: Earlier browser screenshot from before recent edits.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted. Last recorded status: modified `README.md`; untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `index.html`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`.
- Earlier smoke tests verified movement, wolf defeat, gold pickup, and inventory display, but predate recent edits.
- The latest browser-test attempt did not produce results; syntax checking succeeded.
